title: Mitch McConnell, 84, struggles to speak in Senate meeting
text:
By VICTORIA CHURCHILL, US POLITICAL REPORTER

Published:  06:42 AEST, 17 September 2026   |  Updated:  23:54 AEST, 17 September 2026

1.1k

View  comments

Kentucky Republican Senator Mitch McConnell, 84, was recorded visibly struggling to speak during a Wednesday meeting on Capitol Hill.

A glazed-eyed McConnell, who returned to Capitol Hill Monday after an absence of more than 90 days, appears to have been assisted by two colleagues, who told him that it was time to cast a vote, or even what vote to cast during a markup of the Farm Bill. He was instructed to vote 'Aye' on the legislation.

McConnell, who led Republicans in the Senate for nearly two decades, has been dogged by health problems throughout his final term.

He fell on June 14, was briefly hospitalized and had not been seen in public until this week.

In a post on X on Monday, McConnell said his recovery 'has been a long and often frustrating process, and the lingering effects of childhood polio haven't made it any easier.'

'I'm still not quite back to 100%, but I've assured Leader Thune that, as I continue with physical therapy on the advice of my doctors, I will do my best to be present for tough votes when our Conference needs me,' he wrote.

He added that he was 'really looking forward to being back on the Senate floor' and thanked Kentuckians for their well wishes.

Chairman of the Senate Agriculture Committee John Boozman greets Senator Mitch McConnell as he arrives for an Agriculture Committee meeting on Wednesday in Washington, DC. McConnell returned to the Agriculture Committee after a three-month absence, casting a vote to advance the Agricultural Act of 2026

Senator Mitch McConnell talks to his Chief of Staff Terry Carmack during a Senate Agriculture Committee on Wednesday in Washington, DC

McConnell spoke with reporters outside of the US Senate chamber on Monday, but due to Congressional rules, there is no recording allowed in the hallway where he gave remarks. Wednesday's committee meeting was the first time McConnell was widely heard.

Weeks after his hospitalization, he spoke with some of his congressional colleagues by phone and indicated that he was on the mend and looking forward to returning to work soon.

However, both Democrats and Republicans alike were not satisfied with his explanations.

After further pressure mounted to provide 'proof of life,' evidence McConnell released a photo of himself and his wife from the hospital, with a newspaper that was dated July 12, which some initially suspected was AI generated.

He disappeared for weeks after providing the photo, until his office put out a second picture on July 27.

Weeks later, it was revealed that he was discharged from the hospital and would continue his recovery at home.

'Senator McConnell continues his recovery from a fall at home in June,' a comment from his doctor attached to the photograph said.

'Since his discharge from hospital care, he has maintained a strenuous course of physical therapy and rehabilitation.'

Another statement from his office revealed that he had also had a mild case of pneumonia.

McConnell, who is not seeking re-election in this year's midterms, has been dogged by health scares throughout his final term.

Even before his fall earlier this summer, he frighteningly froze in a May hearing on Capitol Hill, raising alarms about his health and even prompting an attack on his staff by President Donald Trump.

Robert Karem, a staffer on the Senate Appropriations Committee's Defense Subcommittee, interrupted McConnell to tell him that Democratic Senators Tammy Baldwin of Wisconsin and Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, as well as Louisiana Republican John Kennedy, all still had questions. The hearing went on for 30 minutes after Karem's interjection.

Karem was attacked by Trump as a 'bum' in a Truth Social post after a clip of the staffer's interaction with the senator made the rounds online.
